chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 71 — Enoch before the Head of Days
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for this concluding vision of the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all seventeen verses: Enoch's ascent through fiery heaven, Michael's disclosure of heavenly secrets, the throne guarded by Seraphim, Cherubim and Ophannim, the appearance of the Head of Days, and the angel's direct address concerning the Son of Man and the peace of the righteous. The source's direct second-person wording in verse 14 is preserved without harmonizing expansion, and no absent speech or transition is supplied between verses 13 and 14. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: After this my spirit was concealed and ascended into the heavens. I saw the sons of the holy angels walking upon flames of fire; their garments were white, their clothing also, and the light of their faces was like snow.
verses.study: Enoch enters a realm where holiness is expressed through fire, white garments and radiant faces. The vision presents heavenly life as purity able to stand within divine brightness.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:9–10 — the heavenly court is marked by white clothing and fire
Matthew 28:3 — the heavenly messenger's appearance is like lightning and clothing like snow

verses.text: I saw two rivers of fire, and the light of that fire shone like hyacinth. Then I fell on my face before the Lord of Spirits.
verses.study: The beauty of the fire does not make the encounter casual. Enoch answers heavenly splendor with bodily humility before the Lord who rules it.
crossReferences: Ezekiel 1:26–28 — radiant heavenly glory causes the prophet to fall
Revelation 1:15–17 — fiery brilliance brings the seer down in awe

verses.text: Michael, one of the chief angels, took me by my right hand, raised me and brought me out to all the hidden things of mercy and the hidden things of righteousness.
verses.study: Michael's guiding hand makes revelation a gift received through heavenly aid. The mysteries disclosed concern mercy and righteousness together, not knowledge detached from moral purpose.
crossReferences: Daniel 10:21 — Michael serves within revealed heavenly purposes
Psalm 85:10 — steadfast love and faithfulness meet righteousness and peace

verses.text: He showed me all the hidden things of the ends of heaven, all the storehouses of the stars and the lights, and every place from which they go out before the holy ones.
verses.study: The ordered lights have storehouses and paths known in heaven. Their regular emergence witnesses to a creation governed rather than abandoned.
crossReferences: Job 38:31–33 — the constellations and ordinances of heaven answer to God
Psalm 19:1–6 — the heavenly lights declare glory through their appointed course

verses.text: The spirit carried Enoch into the heaven of heavens. There I saw, in the midst of that light, something built from crystal stones, and between those stones were tongues of living fire.
verses.study: The third-person naming of Enoch stands within his first-person report, preserving the vision's shifting narration. Crystal and living fire portray a dwelling at once stable, transparent and intensely alive.
crossReferences: Ezekiel 1:22 — an expanse like awe-inspiring crystal appears above the living beings
Revelation 15:2 — the heavenly scene resembles glass mingled with fire

verses.text: My spirit saw a ring encircling that house of fire. On its four sides were rivers full of living fire, and they surrounded that house.
verses.study: Fire encloses the heavenly house on every side. The image communicates complete holiness and protection around the divine dwelling.
crossReferences: Psalm 97:3 — fire goes before the Lord
Zechariah 2:5 — the Lord is a wall of fire around His holy dwelling

verses.text: Around it were Seraphim, Cherubim and Ophannim. These are the ones who do not sleep but guard the throne of his glory.
verses.study: The three orders remain wakeful around the throne. Their ceaseless service contrasts with created beings who abandon their appointed responsibility.
crossReferences: Isaiah 6:2–3 — seraphim attend the holy throne
Ezekiel 10:19–20 — cherubim serve beneath the divine glory
Revelation 4:8 — heavenly guardians praise without rest

verses.text: I saw angels beyond counting—thousands upon thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand—surrounding that house. Michael, Raphael, Gabriel and Phanuel, with the holy angels who are above the heavens, entered and came out of that house.
verses.study: The immeasurable host centers its movement on the heavenly house. Even the named chief angels belong within a greater worshiping order around divine glory.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:10 — thousands upon thousands serve before the throne
Revelation 5:11 — innumerable angels encircle the heavenly throne

verses.text: Michael, Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel came out from that house, with many holy angels who could not be counted.
verses.study: The procession unites the four named angels with an unnumbered multitude. Heavenly leadership remains communal and ordered under the One whose house they serve.
crossReferences: Psalm 103:20–21 — hosts of angels perform the Lord's word
Hebrews 12:22 — innumerable angels gather in the heavenly assembly

verses.text: With them was the Head of Days. His head was like white and pure wool, and his clothing was beyond description.
verses.study: The Head of Days appears in purity and unsearchable majesty. The seer can compare the whiteness of his head but cannot adequately describe his garment.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:9 — the Ancient of Days has clothing like snow and hair like pure wool
1 Timothy 6:16 — divine glory dwells in unapproachable light

verses.text: I fell on my face, and all my flesh melted; my spirit was transformed. I cried out with a loud voice, with a spirit of power, and I blessed, glorified and exalted him.
verses.study: The encounter transforms fear into empowered praise. Enoch's strength does not preserve self-possession; it enables worship after his own power has dissolved.
crossReferences: Daniel 10:8–10 — the prophet loses strength before heavenly glory and is raised
Revelation 1:17 — the seer falls as though dead before the glorious figure

verses.text: These blessings that came from my mouth were pleasing before that Head of Days.
verses.study: Received revelation culminates in acceptable praise. Enoch's words please because they respond faithfully to the glory shown to him.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:14 — words offered before God may be acceptable
Hebrews 13:15 — praise is offered as a continuing sacrifice

verses.text: That Head of Days came with Michael, Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, and with thousands and ten thousand times thousands of angels beyond number.
verses.study: The Head of Days approaches amid both named servants and an immeasurable host. Supreme authority and ordered heavenly service appear together.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 33:2 — the Holy One comes amid myriads
Jude 14–15 — the Lord comes with countless holy ones for judgment

verses.text: That angel came to me, greeted me with his voice and said to me, ‘You are that Son of Man who was born for righteousness. Righteousness has dwelt upon you, and the righteousness of the Head of Days will not forsake you.’
verses.study: The angel's direct address joins the Son of Man title to a calling shaped by righteousness. The verse is allowed to stand in its own wording: birth, indwelling righteousness and the Head of Days' enduring faithfulness define the declaration.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:13–14 — the son of man receives a place in the heavenly court
Isaiah 42:6 — the chosen servant is called and upheld in righteousness

verses.text: He said to me, ‘He calls peace to you in the name of the world that is to come, for from there peace has gone out since the creation of the world; and so it will be for you forever and ever.
verses.study: The promised peace is rooted in creation and reaches into the coming age. It is not a brief escape from conflict but an enduring gift from the heavenly source.
crossReferences: Isaiah 9:6–7 — the ruler's peace has no end
Hebrews 6:5 — the coming age already makes its powers known

verses.text: Everyone who will come and walk in your way, while righteousness never forsakes you, will have their dwelling and their portion with you. They will not be separated from you forever and ever.
verses.study: The righteous way forms a lasting community. Those who walk it receive both dwelling and inheritance, and separation gives way to enduring fellowship.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:6 — the Lord knows the way of the righteous
John 14:2–3 — a prepared dwelling culminates in abiding presence

verses.text: Thus length of days will be with that Son of Man, and peace will be for the righteous; their path will be upright in the name of the Lord of Spirits forever and ever.’
verses.study: The vision closes with life, peace and a straight path. The Son of Man's enduring days provide the setting in which the righteous remain rightly directed under the Lord of Spirits.
crossReferences: Psalm 21:4 — enduring length of days is granted by God
Isaiah 26:7 — the path of the righteous is made level
John 5:26 — life is granted to the Son

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 71 carries Enoch into the heaven of heavens. Rivers of fire, crystal stones and living flame reveal a holy dwelling before which the proper response is humility and praise.
Michael guides Enoch through mysteries of mercy, righteousness and the created lights. Revelation remains relational and ethical: it is received by grace and ordered toward faithful understanding.
The throne scene gathers Seraphim, Cherubim, Ophannim and innumerable angels around the Head of Days. Their unceasing service displays a heavenly order centered entirely on divine glory.

The concluding address binds the Son of Man, righteousness, peace and the coming age together. Without adding an absent explanation, the text promises lasting dwelling and an upright path to those who share the way of righteousness.

crossReferences: Isaiah 6:1–7 — fiery throne attendants and transformed worship
Ezekiel 1:22–28 — crystal, fire and the appearance of divine glory
Daniel 7:9–14 — the Ancient of Days, countless attendants and son of man
Hebrews 12:22–24 — the innumerable heavenly assembly
Revelation 4:2–8 — ceaseless throne worship
Revelation 5:11–13 — the unnumbered host blesses the enthroned One
